info.description: Using the API for the CRM service, you can integrate your system with CRM from SendPulse and receive detailed information on pipelines, deals, contacts, companies, tasks, products and their attributes and users. You can also create and update deals, contacts, companies and tasks, assign and remove fields, tags, contact details and instant messengers. Requests are authorized with an OAuth2 access token (client credentials flow): obtain it at https://api.sendpulse.com/oauth/access_token with the ID and Secret from your account and pass it in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. On this page, click "Authorize", insert the ID and Secret, then use "Try it out" within each method block.
info.title: SendPulse CRM Public API

post.description: Attaches a file uploaded to the file manager to a deal, contact, company, task or comment.
post.x-ai-description: This endpoint links a file previously uploaded to the File Manager to a specific CRM entity (deal, contact, company, task, or comment). The attachment itself is a relational record: the binary file must already exist in the File Manager, and this call only creates the association between that file and the target entity. Use it to enrich CRM records with supporting documents (contracts, invoices, screenshots) so they are accessible in the context of the related business object.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Ensure the file has already been uploaded to the File Manager and that you have its file identifier before calling this endpoint; this operation attaches an existing file, it does not upload one.
Confirm the target entity type (deal, contact, company, task, or comment) and its ID exist to avoid orphaned or failed attachments.
Validate the request body against CreateAttachmentRequest; a 422 response indicates missing or invalid fields such as an unknown entity type or file reference.
If a 403 is returned, check that the account has permission to modify the target entity.
x-ai-responding-instructions: On success, confirm the attachment was created and reference the returned attachment ID from the data object.
Mention which entity the file is now attached to so the user can verify the correct association.
If a 422 validation error occurs, explain which field is invalid (e.g., unknown entity type or missing file reference).
If a 401 or 403 occurs, clarify whether it is an authentication or a permission issue.
x-ai-suggestions: Upload the file to the File Manager first if it does not yet exist, then reference it here.
After attaching, retrieve the entity to confirm the attachment appears in its list of files.
Attach supporting documents such as signed contracts or invoices to deals for better record keeping.

post.description: Attaches several files to entities.
post.x-ai-description: This endpoint attaches multiple files to CRM entities (deals, contacts, companies) in a single request. Use it to associate documents, images, or other assets with records in bulk, which is far more efficient than creating attachments one by one. Each item in the batch is an independent attachment linking a stored file to a target entity, so a single call can distribute files across several different entities at once.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Ensure each file referenced in the batch has already been uploaded/stored and you hold a valid file identifier before attaching.
Confirm every target entity (type and ID) exists and the account has permission to modify it; a wrong entity reference will cause a 422 ValidationFailed.
Prefer this batch endpoint over repeated single-attachment calls when linking more than one file to reduce request overhead and rate-limit pressure.
Validate that the `attachments` array is non-empty and that each item conforms to CreateAttachmentRequest before sending.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Report how many attachments were created and list the returned attachment IDs from the `data` array.
If the response is partial or ambiguous, map each created record back to its source file and target entity so the user can verify coverage.
On 422, explain which attachment items failed validation (e.g. missing file reference or invalid entity) rather than reporting a generic error.
On 401/403, clarify whether the issue is authentication (token) or insufficient permissions for the target entities.
x-ai-suggestions: Verify the attachments appear on their entities using the corresponding list/get attachments operation.
If any item failed validation, resubmit only the corrected attachment items.
Consider cleaning up orphaned uploaded files that were not successfully attached.

delete.description: Removes the attachment from the entity.

confirmation.body: This will permanently delete the attachment. This action cannot be undone.
confirmation.title: Delete attachment

delete.x-ai-description: Permanently removes a file attachment from its parent entity (deal, contact, or company). This is a destructive, irreversible action: the stored file is detached and deleted, not archived. Use it to clean up outdated or mistakenly uploaded documents, but treat it as a point of no return — there is no undo endpoint to restore a deleted attachment.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Confirm you have the correct attachmentId; verify the attachment exists and belongs to the intended entity before deleting to avoid removing the wrong file.
Because deletion is irreversible, always obtain explicit user confirmation before calling this endpoint.
Expect an empty 204 response on success; do not wait for or parse a response body.
Handle 404 as an already-removed or non-existent attachment, and 403 as insufficient permissions rather than retrying blindly.
x-ai-responding-instructions: On a 204 response, confirm clearly that the attachment was permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
If a 404 is returned, explain that the attachment no longer exists or was already removed.
If a 403 is returned, explain that the account lacks permission to delete this attachment.
Avoid implying the file can be restored — there is no recovery option.
x-ai-suggestions: Download or back up the attachment before deletion if the user may need it later.
After deletion, refresh the entity's attachment list to reflect the change.

get.description: Returns active task boards available to the user, with their steps, task attributes and settings.
get.x-ai-description: Retrieves all active task boards accessible to the authenticated user. In SendPulse, a board is the top-level container that organizes work into pipeline steps (stages) and defines the task attributes and settings shared by its cards. Use this endpoint first to discover available board IDs and their step structure before querying, creating, or moving tasks, since every downstream task operation is scoped to a specific board and step.

Do not assume a board exists; verify it appears in the returned list and is active.
When the user refers to a board by name, map that name to its ID from this response rather than guessing.
Inspect each board's steps and task attributes to understand the pipeline structure before creating or moving tasks.
If the list is empty, conclude the account has no boards yet rather than treating it as an error.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Present boards as a concise list using their names, and keep the numeric IDs available for follow-up actions.
Summarize each board's pipeline by naming its steps in order so the user understands the workflow.
If no boards are returned, state clearly that none exist and suggest creating one.
On a 401, explain the token is missing or expired; on a 403, explain the user lacks access to boards.

Review the board's task attributes before building task payloads to match the expected fields.

put.x-ai-description: Updates a single stored value of a task attribute (custom field) on a CRM board. In SendPulse CRM, attributes hold structured data attached to a task (e.g. city, budget, stage); each attribute may carry one or more values, and this endpoint overwrites one specific value identified by valueId. Use it to correct or refresh existing data on a task without recreating the attribute.
x-ai-reasoning-instructions: Resolve valueId first by calling the 'Get a task by ID' operation and reading attributes[].values[].id; never guess the identifier.
Confirm that boardId, attributeId, and valueId belong to the same task and attribute chain to avoid updating the wrong record.
Match the type of the new value (string, number, or boolean) to the attribute's defined data type to prevent validation errors (422).
If the value does not yet exist, add a new value instead of calling this update endpoint.
x-ai-responding-instructions: Confirm the update succeeded and restate which attribute and value were changed.
If a 404 is returned, explain that the board, attribute, or value identifier was not found and suggest re-fetching the task.
If a 422 is returned, explain that the submitted value failed validation (likely a type mismatch) and show the expected format.
Suggest re-fetching the task to display the refreshed attribute state.
